title: ScreenConnect RMM+ extension default/blank API secret (CVE-2026-127063) abused to push rogue clients and SCKit to managed endpoints
why: ConnectWise (as CNA) assigned CVE-2026-127063 on Nov 12 to the RMM+ extension's default static API secret. Huntress links the Nov 11 SCKit incident (288 endpoints, 48 orgs, commands with no matching logins) to RMM+ 1.0.31/1.0.32 accepting a blank key. ConnectWise disabled RMM+ in about 400 partner environments. No fixed RMM+ version exists. CVE-2026-127063 is not in CISA KEV (the earlier KEV entry CVE-2026-84869 covers only the client spread step), and there is no Microsoft guidance. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: ConnectWise disclosure still says no fixed RMM+ version; not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries). Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: On on-prem ScreenConnect, disable and uninstall RMM+ and related extensions now. Review Run Command and Toolbox history since Nov 11 for mass commands or ScreenConnect installer downloads. Make sure technician clients are on 26.6.5 or later.
product: DataComm RMM+ third-party extension for ConnectWise ScreenConnect (Huntress: 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accept a blank key); no fixed version announced

title: LiteLLM MCP command injection + Starlette BadHost (CVE-2026-42271/CVE-2026-48710): renewed honeypot scanning (SANS ISC)
why: Not ahead: CISA added CVE-2026-42271 to KEV on June 8, 2026 and CVE-2026-48710 on Sept 2, 2026. SANS ISC (Nov 16) reports new weekend requests to /mcp-rest/test/tools/list on its honeypots, so the chain is still being sprayed.
action: Upgrade LiteLLM to 1.83.7+ and Starlette to 1.0.1+, block POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and /mcp-rest/test/tools/list at the proxy, and rotate stored provider keys on any exposed instance.
product: LiteLLM 1.74.2 through 1.83.6 with Starlette 1.0.0 or earlier

title: wfx-loot: 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts push a CI secret stealer; secrets taken from 1,800+ repos, with AWS and Entra ID persistence
why: Aikido, OX Security, SafeDep and StepSecurity report a live campaign since Nov 10: stolen tokens for 4,837 GitHub accounts opened ~62-66k probe PRs and the stealer ran in at least 1,806 repositories, still ongoing on Nov 12 with exfil moved to Telegram. The payload adds wfx-ci-* federated credentials to Entra ID apps and rewrites AWS role trust policies, which survive secret rotation. There is no CVE (no product bug), so no CISA KEV entry, and no Microsoft or GitHub guidance appeared in the sources reviewed. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Search your GitHub org for PRs titled "docs: dependency audit notes" or wfx-docs branches since Nov 10; for any hit revoke that account's tokens and rotate every secret its workflows could reach, then hunt Entra ID for federated credentials named wfx-ci-* and AWS sessions named wfx-*.
vendor: GitHub (abuse of stolen developer tokens; no product flaw)
product: GitHub Actions workflows and npm postinstall hooks in any repository a compromised account can write to (since Nov 10, 2026)

title: PostgreSQL CVE-2026-6460 type confusion: low-privileged database user to OS code execution, RCE technique now public
why: Researcher Mehmet Ince published a write-up turning the 22-year-old type confusion into code execution, and an independent researcher reproduced the crash with four SQL statements as a zero-privilege role (dev.to); the item hit Hacker News today. OffSeq and SecurityOnline report no exploitation, and it is not in CISA KEV. Hosted PostgreSQL services may be exposed, but no cloud-provider statement was found. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade to PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 or 14.25 (14 is now end-of-life), prioritising multi-tenant servers, and until then remove CREATE privileges from untrusted roles.
product: PostgreSQL before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25 (part of a 52-CVE release on Nov 12, 2026)

title: GeoVision GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 hosts exploited to deploy XMRig at 13 organizations (likely known unauthenticated WebCam Server RCE)
why: Huntress SOC saw attackers abuse internet-exposed GeoVision GV-VMS at 13 organizations (most activity Nov 8-10): commands spawned by GeoStartupAgentService.exe as SYSTEM, a BYOVD driver and IFEO hijacks to disable Microsoft Defender, then a DHT/PKARR Go loader and XMRig. Huntress told Help Net Security (Nov 16) that the sampled hosts ran GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 and that one of three unauthenticated RCEs in GeoVision's April 2026 advisory is the most likely entry point, but the exact CVE is not confirmed. No CVE for this activity is in CISA KEV and there is no Microsoft guidance; the campaign actively tries to switch Defender off.
action: Upgrade GV-VMS to V17.4.8.58 or later, take GeoVision management interfaces off the internet (VPN/IP allowlist), and hunt for cmd/PowerShell children of GeoStartupAgentService.exe and IFEO Debugger keys on Defender processes.
product: GeoVision GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 (older than fixed V17.4.8.58)

title: Apify breach (Nov 9-10): attacker accessed internal systems; customer billing data and 2FA recovery codes exposed, all API tokens rotated
why: Apify's status page confirms an unauthorized third party accessed internal systems on Nov 9-10, detected Nov 11. Customer notices report exposed emails, billing details and 2FA recovery codes, and some GitHub OAuth connections were revoked. There is no CVE, so nothing is in KEV, and no Microsoft coverage was seen. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Replace Apify API tokens in every pipeline, set up 2FA again, review GitHub activity for any account linked to Apify, and warn finance about invoice phishing that uses real billing details.
product: Apify platform (hosted)

title: Fortinet FortiOS November batch: unauthenticated super-admin command execution via HA packets (126259) plus OSPF/BGP routing flaws
why: Fortinet published FG-IR-26-273 on Nov 10 (CVSS 9.8 per NVD). Its HA virtual patch is labelled '0day', and its own scores mark some bugs as having exploit code. Fortinet reports no attacks, there is no public PoC, and none of the batch is in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade FortiOS to 8.0.1, or to 7.6.8/7.4.13/7.2.14 when they ship. Until then, apply the FortiGuard HA virtual patch and keep HA/FGSP sync traffic on a dedicated non-routed segment.
product: FortiOS 8.0.0, 7.6.0-7.6.7, 7.4.0-7.4.12, 7.2.0-7.2.13 (HA FGSP with standalone-config-sync, or autoscale)

title: Fortinet FortiMail unauthenticated RCE: path traversal (126147), HA join-request command injection (126148), SMTP format string (126163)
why: Fortinet advisories FG-IR-26-199/200 (Nov 10, CVSS 9.8) list these as unauthenticated code execution and 'Known Exploited: No'. Rescana confirmed they were not in CISA KEV on Nov 11. A GitHub 'PoC' for 126147 indexed on Sploitus is only a simulated lab, not a working exploit against FortiMail. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade FortiMail to 8.0.2/7.6.7/7.4.9 (migrate off 7.2), and restrict the management interface and HA ports to trusted networks.

title: Synology DSM pre-auth SQL injection in Auth API (9.8) and rsync auth bypass allow unauthenticated arbitrary file read/write
why: Synology SA-26:19 (Nov 10, CVE published Nov 12) fixes an unauthenticated SQL injection with arbitrary file write. Viettel, who reported it, calls it a pre-auth zero-click RCE. No exploitation or public PoC yet and not in CISA KEV, while Synology NAS devices are already being hit by ransomware via an older DSM flaw. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Update DSM to 7.2.1-69057-13 / 7.2.2-72806-10 / 7.3.2-86009-5 / 7.4.1-90080-1 or later, and keep DSM (ports 5000/5001) and rsync off the internet.

title: Citrix NetScaler November fixes: Console unauth bypass (CVE-2026-120869, 9.4) and default-config ADC/Gateway memory overflow (CVE-2026-120868, 9.3)
why: Citrix bulletins (Nov 11-12) fix an unauthenticated Console auth bypass and a packet-processing overflow that affects every ADC/Gateway, default config included. watchTowr is building exposure checks. Citrix reports no exploitation, no confirmed public PoC exists, and none of these CVEs is in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade internet-facing NetScaler ADC/Gateway to 14.1-73.57 or 13.1-64.39 and NetScaler Console to 14.1-74.34. Until then, restrict Console access to management hosts.
product: NetScaler ADC/Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-73.57, 13.1 before 13.1-64.39; NetScaler Console before 14.1-74.34

title: Red Hat Quay unauthenticated signing-key takeover (CVE-2026-123710, 9.8) plus cross-tenant robot-token theft (CVE-2026-110697); no fixed release named
why: Red Hat disclosed the bug on Nov 11. An anonymous /v2/auth token can authorize service-key rotation, letting an attacker install a non-expiring signing key and forge tokens for every repository. Upstream fixes were merged Nov 11, but no fixed release was named as of reporting. There is no PoC or ITW report, and it is not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Block /keys at the proxy so only trusted internal components can reach it. Review service_key_rotate audit events for keys with no expiration and remove any you don't recognize.
product: Red Hat Quay 3 and Quay 5 (standalone, Quay Operator on OpenShift, mirror registry for OpenShift); exposed when /keys is reachable by untrusted clients

title: Apache Shiro DefaultLdapRealm accepts any password when authentication caching is enabled (CVE-2026-129349)
why: Apache disclosed it on oss-security on Nov 13 (CVSS 4.0 9.1, network, no privileges). It is a Java library, not a Microsoft product, and it is not in CISA KEV. No public PoC or exploitation reported. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Find Java apps that bundle shiro-core with an LDAP realm and upgrade them to 3.0.2. Until then, turn off authentication caching on those realms.
product: Apache Shiro (shiro-core) before 3.0.1

title: Apache APISIX 3.20.0 fixes 7 flaws, incl. unauthenticated route-auth bypass (CVE-2026-124680) and identity-header spoofing (CVE-2026-124679)
why: Apache posted seven APISIX advisories on oss-security on Nov 13. Two let unauthenticated clients get past authentication in certain configurations. Not a Microsoft product, not in CISA KEV, and no public PoC or exploitation reported. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade APISIX gateways to 3.20.0. Until then, check for routes without auth that share an upstream with protected routes, and turn off forward-auth allow_degradation.
product: Apache APISIX 0.9 through 3.19.0 (124680); 3.18.0 through 3.19.0 (124679)

title: Cyrus SASL SRP mechanism authentication bypass: A=N forces zero shared secret (CVE-2026-129483)
why: VulnCheck (CNA) published it Nov 15 with an upstream fix commit and oss-security post; CVSS 9.1/9.3, network, no privileges. No exploitation reported and not in CISA KEV. Only servers that enable the SRP SASL mechanism are exposed. A Microsoft CSAF/VEX record exists for the package, but no Microsoft product guidance.
action: Check whether any service offers the SRP SASL mechanism (mech_list / installed libsrp plugin) and disable or remove the SRP plugin until distro packages carry upstream commit fb3724f.
product: Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 (SRP server mechanism)

title: Node.js November 2026 security release: 16 CVEs incl. HTTPS cross-connection memory leak exposing TLS private keys (CVE-2026-123864)
why: Node.js shipped 16 fixes on Nov 11, seven rated High. CVE-2026-123864 lets an unauthenticated client read other connections' memory, including TLS private keys, and several HTTP/2 bugs let a client crash default servers. No exploitation or public PoC reported, and none are in KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade to Node.js 22.23.5/24.22.3/26.13.1, rebuild container images, and consider rotating TLS keys on HTTPS services that ran affected handlers.
product: Node.js 22.x before 22.23.5, 24.x before 24.22.3, 26.x before 26.13.1 (end-of-life lines always affected)

why: Zoom bulletins ZSB-26023/24 (Nov 10) rate 108186 Critical 9.6 with user interaction required. No exploitation or public PoC and not in CISA KEV. This is a Windows app but not a Microsoft product, so no MSRC advisory applies. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.

product: Zoom Workplace for Windows 7.1.0 before 7.1.8 (108186); before 7.1.5 (108187)

title: NoisyTCP: Linux kernel TCP pre-auth remote crash (CVE-2026-99288), present since 4.4, full details public after embargo
why: Hyunwoo Kim posted the full NoisyTCP write-up to oss-security on Nov 15 once the linux-distros embargo ended. A remote attacker with no login can panic any Linux host that has a TCP listener and spreads packets over 2+ RX queues or RPS (default on most cloud VMs). Kim has a private lab PoC (5 s to 2 min against KVM guests), but no exploit code is public and nobody has reported attacks. Debian and Oracle UEK have fixed kernels. As of Nov 15-16, Ubuntu and RHEL/Rocky/Alma had no fix yet. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft/MSRC (Azure Linux) entry in the collected data. Scored low because the impact is DoS only: Red Hat 7.5, no NVD score. Nov 16 update: BleepingComputer and others now cover it; Debian and Arch ship fixed kernels, Ubuntu and RHEL trackers still list it as unfixed/affected; researcher has still not published exploit code and no attacks are reported. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Patch internet-facing Linux hosts to a kernel with commit 4e2b3ef19e0e (6.12.117/6.18.63/7.3.4 or your distro backport) and reboot. Until a distro fix ships, Ubuntu/RHEL hosts can set net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=0 in every netns, or use a single RX queue with RPS/RFS off. Weigh the SYN-flood trade-off first.
product: Linux kernel 4.4 through 6.12.116, 6.13-6.18.62, 6.19-7.3.3 (TCP established-socket lookup); EOL 7.2 gets no fix

title: 'Hello Again': fTPM lockout rollback via RPMC flaws lets attackers with physical access brute-force Windows Hello and BitLocker TPM+PIN
why: Academic paper (arXiv 2611.18126, CCS '26, Nov 13) demonstrates end-to-end on locked hardware: a 4-digit Hello PIN in 40 hours, BitLocker 6-digit TPM+PIN worst case 20 days, by rolling back fTPM anti-hammering state (Winbond RPMC HMAC key leak via glitching; AMD controller not verifying increments; some AMD boards with no rollback protection). Per the authors, no vendor committed to a root-cause fix; Microsoft only raised its recommended minimum Hello PIN to 6 digits. No CVE, no MSRC advisory.
action: For lost/stolen-device risk, enforce Windows Hello and BitLocker pre-boot PINs of at least 6 (preferably 8+) digits or alphanumeric PINs via policy.
product: Windows Hello and BitLocker TPM+PIN on x86 systems using firmware TPMs (AMD, Intel, Pluton) backed by SPI flash

title: Copeland/Dixell XWEB EVO (EOL) batch: pre-auth root command injection and hardcoded backdoor password (CVE-2026-124002..124015)
why: VulnCheck published a batch of 14 XWEB EVO CVEs on Nov 12, including unauthenticated root command injection (CVSS 9.8) and a hardcoded admin backdoor password. This comes while the sibling XWEB PRO (CVE-2026-25085) is being exploited in refrigeration sabotage. There is no public exploit and no reported in-the-wild use, and none of the CVEs is in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14). Rechecked Nov 16: no new CISA KEV entries this run; still not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 16 17Z: collector saw no new CISA KEV or MSRC entries this run; still not in KEV.
action: Take XWEB EVO web interfaces off the internet now, put them behind VPN or allowlists, and plan to replace these end-of-service units.
product: XWEB EVO refrigeration/HVAC supervisor, 4.3.0 through 5.8.8 depending on CVE; product line end of service March 2026

title: Dassault 3DEXPERIENCE Station Launcher App: unauthenticated deserialization RCE (CVSS 10.0) plus two command injections
why: Vendor (3DS CNA) advisories published Nov 16: CVE-2026-93664 unauthenticated deserialization RCE (CVSS 10.0) and CVE-2026-77033/19732 OS command injection. No public exploit or exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV.
action: Apply the fix packs named in the 3DS advisories for CVE-2026-93664/77033/19732 and restrict network access to Station Launcher services.
product: 3DEXPERIENCE platform Station Launcher App, R2023x through R2026x
